This rugged rifle is essentially an Israeli version of the venerable AK47. It has the same solid all-around performance with a slightly faster rate of fire and a bigger punch.
A workhorse of armies, militias, and terror groups all over the world, the AK47 is an incredibly reliable weapon that neither falters nor excels in any one category.
The F1 is a bullpup assault rifle from France that fires in 3-round bursts. It has above average accuracy and is ideal for those who prefer a high rate of fire over raw power.
The MS16 has exceptional range, power, and accuracy for an assault rifle, but it requires a skilled user to deploy it effectively due to its semi-automatic action.
The P416 is a modern take on a classic weapon. It has a blistering rate of fire and solid accuracy.
This Swiss-made assault rifle has a higher-than-average rate of fire along with decent accuracy and average damage.
This small caliber handgun is ideal for stealth when fitted with a sound suppressor. It is exceptionally accurate at close range and can be used while on a zipline.
This hand cannon gives unmatched short-range power and can be used while on a zipline. Strong hands are needed to deal with its massive recoil.
An American-made revolver that packs some serious punch at close range but has limited ammo capacity. It can be used while on a zipline.
A classic .45 caliber semi-automatic handgun that can be used while on a zipline. It’s a solid all-around performer at short range.
This grenade launcher holds 4 rounds of 40mm grenades that will explode on impact.
This classic weapon really needs no introduction. The RPG-7 can be used to take out vehicles, structures, and concentrated groups of enemies at almost any range.
The MKG has an incredibly high rate of fire and excels at sending as much lead downrange as possible.
The PKM is a powerful, light machinegun with solid accuracy and range. It carries a massive 100-round box of ammo, but takes time to reload.
A light machinegun from Singapore that handles well and has even performance across the chart. It straddles the line between assault rifle and LMG and is also quick to reload.
A classic lever-action shotgun that is devastating in close quarters. This variant has a 28-inch barrel which gives it slightly more range than other shotguns.
The M133 is a pump-action shotgun with a shorter barrel that disperses buckshot in a wider pattern. It excels at clearing out rooms and hits hard close up.
This Italian semi-automatic shotgun can be fired quickly, but requires the user to be more diligent with their aim than with other shotguns.
The A2000 is an average performer across the board, neither excelling nor faltering in any category when compared to other weapons in its class.
The BZ19 has solid power and accuracy. It doesn’t have the fastest rate of fire in its class, but it does feature a large-capacity magazine capable of holding 64 rounds.
The Vector .45 ACP is a more recent design that enables an extremely high rate of fire without all the troublesome recoil. It’s accurate and handles well in close quarters combat.
The MP5 is renowned for solid accuracy, good handling, and a high rate of fire.
This small machine pistol rapidly fires low caliber rounds with minimal recoil. It can be also be used while on a zipline.
Unmatched in both range and accuracy, this bolt-action sniper rifle can take down distant targets with ease. Just keep its low rate of fire in mind.
This battle-tested Soviet Bloc semi-automatic sniper rifle allows for quick follow-up shots at the expense of some accuracy and range.
No rifle hits harder at long range than this .50 caliber beast. Simply put, it kills what it hits.
The recurve bow packs a big punch for such a low-tech weapon. It's useful for hunting both man and beast, and can be outfitted with explosive or flaming arrows.
Flare guns can be used to set things on fire from a distance, take out enemy personnel, or to create distractions. Just remember that they’re single-shot weapons.
The flamethrower is an incredibly destructive weapon that can lay waste to anything flammable. Use carefully to avoide getting burned.
A customized 1911 pistol with a larger magazine, silencer, and custom paint. Enhanced for accuracy and stealth.
A customized .44 Magnum with extended barrel, optical sight, 6 round chamber, and custom paint. Enhanced for accuracy and damage.
A customized Vector .45 ACP with reflex sight, suppressor, extended magazine, and custom paint. Enhanced for accuracy and damage.
A customized M133 shotgun with extended shell capacity, and custom paint. Enhanced for damage.
A customized P416 with optical scope, extended magazine, suppressor, and custom paint. Enhanced for accuracy and damage.
A customized MKG with optical scope, extended magazine, and custom paint. Enhanced for accuracy, damage, and low recoil.
A customized Z93 with extended magazine, high power scope, and custom paint. Fires an explosive, penetrating round. Enhanced for damage at long range.
This highly modified recurve bow is for users who like to stick out from the crowd. It can be outfitted with explosive or flaming arrows.
An M-700 decked out with all the latest modifications to make it more stable, more accurate, and more powerful.
A Japanese flare gun re-purposed as a single-shot shotgun. Dangerous at close range.
Machetes are a common sight in the jungle. They can be used for everything from cutting through thick brush to killing people and animals.
The tanto is a Japanese dagger that was carried by the samurai. Wielding one of these will increase the damage dealt in melee combat.
This ancient blade was forged on Rook Island hundreds of years ago. Rakyat warriors have used it to end countless lives since then.

An Ace of Clubs, one of the edges slightly nicked. Good for cheating at a poker game.
Looks like a small carving of a boar, someone must have a thing for them.
A lovingly carved miniature shark, much less intimidating than the real thing.
A detailed carving of a spider, keep away from arachnophobes.
This carving of a heron was beautifully carved by someone with real talent.
A colorful set of crayons, an unexpected find in these parts.
Cigarettes. Probably as valuable here as they would be in a prison.
These islands are crawling with bugs, bet someone will happily pay for this bug spray.
An ornately detailed ceremonial knife, it's original use is likely long forgotten.
A flask of bootleg alcohol. Distilled locally and strong enough to blind a goat.
A bootleg DVD with 'XXX' scrawled on it in felt tip. It's been played a lot of times.
A knock-off "Cuban" cigar, more filler weed than quality tobacco.
A fake piece of ID? Who the hell cards in this part of the world?
A tattered porno mag with stuck pages and far too much mileage. Handle with care.
A day-old marijuana joint, half smoked and still pungent.
Counterfeit money with flattened zeroes. Perhaps printed from the Shah of Iran's missing printing press?
A small bag of dried hallucinogenic mushrooms. Barely strong enough to spice a salad.
Ivory carving, illegal but beautifully made.
A rare African conflict diamond, probably brought over by a mercenary. It's sure to fetch a pretty penny.
Chocolate. Full of calories but way past its expiration date.
Toothpaste. Good to see someone still cares about dental hygiene out here.
Water purification pills, vital for staying hydrated without getting the runs.
A disposable light stick, with so many caves here, someone will want this.
Crystal Meth, the poor man's cocaine. It's purity is questionable.
Glue, around these parts it's more likely to be used as recreation rather than for its intended purpose.
A small bottle of amphetamines, with a hand-written label: "Here's the top shit I promised. Enjoy ;-) L."
A shark tooth necklace, likely of Māori origins.
Bright orange traffic cone with reflective stripes. The hallmark of any good night out.
An oversized feather. What it is doing here is a mystery.
A picture of a naked dwarf, laughing and pointing at the camera. And he's not using his fingers.
It's a rusty trombone! Who knew that was real!
Why would someone place these pink and fuzzy stripper handcuffs here? Scratch that, do you really want to know?
An old teddy bear, eye missing and a musty smell. Stuffing is visible between the stitches. A worn, ripped label names the bear "Bo B--".
A mini flashlight like this would likely be a sought-after item in these parts.
A set of dog tags, probably from some merc who wanted to remember his years in the military when he meant something.
A paper bag, damp with red spots and buzzing with flies. You can sell that. Sure.
A pair of plastic sunglasses, shuttered like they fell out of an 80s music video. Tragically mismatched in this hell.
The head of a doll with creepy oversized eyes, both its body and owner were likely lost long ago.
Someone's lucky lighter. It's little more than a trinket now that it's out of lighter fuel.
A simple beaded necklace most likely made by one of the locals.
A half crumpled pack of cigarettes. Looks like someone wanted to quit but changed his mind.
It won't be hard to find a buyer for this beautiful seashell.
Maybe you can sell this keycard. It is a little shiny.
An ornately carved wooden trinket box, empty, but with a fine velvet interior.
A solid gold pocket watch, still working, but the gears are running slow.
My tracking device will probably fetch a good price at the store, just say it's an MP3 player.
A torn piece of a strange-looking document. Perhaps it will make sense when all the pieces are assembled.
A torn piece of a strange-looking document. Perhaps it will make sense when all the pieces are assembled.
A torn piece of a strange-looking document. Perhaps it will make sense when all the pieces are assembled.
A torn piece of a strange-looking document. Perhaps it will make sense when all the pieces are assembled.
Radio frequency codes for the Medusa's radio system.
Radio frequency codes for the Medusa's radio system.
A key to the control room of the Medusa.
Chinese jade can date back to Neolithic times, too bad no one on Rook Island knows what that means. Still, it should be worth some cash.
Ancient Chinese coins can be up to 2,500 years old. Who knows how old the ones on Rook Island are.
The Chinese sure love their dragons. Did you know that it’s the only mythical creature on the Chinese zodiac?
Bronze working started in the Xia Dynasty, maybe that little fact will get you a few more bucks for this when you sell this.
These things were the earliest form of money used in China. Fitting as now you can sell it and get some decent cash.
The Six Noble Arts of the Zhou dynasty list archery as a skill worthy of the emperor. This arrowhead is worthy of whatever you can sell it for.
This pot likely predates more exquisite porcelain wares, but you can probably still sell it for some cold hard cash.
Your typical example of Chinese porcelain, or “China” as some folks call it. This would sell for a mint in the states, but expect less around these parts.
A crude but old Chinese bowl, it’s probably seen a lot of noodles in its time. You should be able to get some cash for it.
Sancai translates into “three colors.” This little statuette used to fit well into that category, but time and age have turned it into a “one-cai.”
This decorative wall plaque would make any antique collector giddy, too bad there aren’t any around Rook Island.
A smaller version of a soldier from the famous Terracotta Army, it may look like a cheap tourist item, but it’s the genuine article.
Chances are, some important Chinese figure rests within, but there’s no way to confirm that. Just sell it and be done with it.
These were used to dilute ink when writing calligraphy or painting. Surely someone here will pay to take it off your hands.
Chinese medicine can include everything from ginseng to powdered tiger bones. A person who believes in that stuff will buy anything.
A smaller leaf, amber in color with a musty aroma. Use it to craft Hunting syringes.
This dark green leaf has many veins and a faint earthy smell. Use it to craft Medical syringes.
A thin crimson-colored leaf that emits a sweet rosy smell. Use it to craft Combat syringes.
A light blue leaf with a ragged edge. Use it craft Exploration syringes.
A perfectly formed, pure white leaf. Use it to craft Special syringes.
This boar hide is tough enough to use in a few crafting recipes.
Komodo dragons poison victims through their saliva, but this skin is clean and safe enough to use for crafting.
This is a fine example of Blood Komodo dragon hide. <font color="#fab945">Cannot be discarded or sold: must be used for crafting.</font>
Deer hide is tough to come by because of how hard the buggers are to catch, pardon my french, but now that you've done it, go ahead and use the hide for crafting.
This beautiful Spotted Sika hide is a rare specimen indeed. It will fetch a fine price at the store.
It's goat skin, nothing more, nothing less, but definitely useful for crafting a few things.
Pork crackling is a local delicacy, and for good reason, but you should save this skin for crafting instead.
Cassowaries are tough; honor these foes by using their leather to craft something.
An excellent specimen of cassowary leather. <font color="#fab945">Cannot be discarded or sold: must be used for crafting.</font>
The thylacine is classified as extinct, so congratulations on finding one and making it more extinct. If you sell it quickly no one will probably notice.
Shark skin is versatile but tough to come by for obvious reasons. <font color="#fab945">Cannot be discarded or sold: must be used for crafting.</font>
Albino crocodile leather is tough and exquisitely textured. You'll definitely profit from its sale.
This tortoise may have lived for hundreds of years, but now it's going to be used for god knows what when you sell it.
There's more skin on this thing than you'd think. You'll be able to craft something with it for sure.
Now this is an excellent example of white belly tapir skin. <font color="#fab945">Cannot be discarded or sold: must be used for crafting.</font>
This dog was rabid, no doubt, but by carefully removing the skin you'll have something worth crafting with.
The chances of this leopard skin ultimately ending up in New Jersey are about 50/50, if you don't craft with it.
This black panther skin is a rare find indeed. <font color="#fab945">Cannot be discarded or sold: must be used for crafting.</font>
Buffalo hide is plentiful and versatile, and good for crafting with.
Buffalo hide of good quality like this is rare. <font color="#fab945">Cannot be discarded or sold: must be used for crafting.</font>
Finally, a disease-free macaque - sell this skin at the earliest opportunity.
Bet you could make a nice rug out of this, but it'd be a pain to clean. You're better off crafting with it instead.
It was a tough battle to get this skin, so wear it with pride by crafting it into something useful. <font color="#fab945">Cannot be discarded or sold.</font>
Skinning a tiger is no easy feat, but the crafting potential will make it worthwhile.
This rare tiger skin is one-of-a-kind. It's too precious to sell. <font color="#fab945">Cannot be discarded or sold: must be used for crafting.</font>
This a decent strip of leathery skin, and it should fetch a good price at the store.
Shells are hard and durable, you can definitely profit from them at the store.
Feathers have a surprising number of uses, just ask the ancient Romans. But really, you should just sell them.
Shark skin, fresh from the beast, and ready for crafting.
This pelt may smell faintly of urine, but don't let that put you off making use of it for crafting.
Part of the loot from Yamashita's fabled WWII bounty. Who knows what treasures he stole from across Asia and where the Golden Lilies hid them.
Another cache of Yamashita's fabled WWII bounty, hidden in a WWII ammo crate and stamped with the Golden Lily.
Rumor has it that someone on the island's paying fine coin for Yamashita's fabled WWII bounty.
Another cache of Yamashita's fabled WWII bounty, secreted in an ammo case and likely secreted here by a Golden Lily transport before the end of WWII.
A letter from a Japanese soldier during WWII, passed from friend to friend until there was nobody left to carry them.
One of the Japanese letters from WWII, from a time when the war was at its most desperate.
Another Japanese letter, stained and almost illegible from years of neglect.

Get the best five-card combination using the two cards you hold and the cards on the table (the board).

The opportunity for each player at the table to take action after the Hole Cards, the Flop, the Turn and the River have been dealt. Actions are taken in a clockwise direction around the table. Each round of betting ends once all remaining players have taken action and have had the chance to reach to another player's RAISE or an ALL-IN bet.
You can leave the table at any time during the game with the amount of money you currently have in your balance. Any money that has already been put into the pot is forfeited upon leaving the table.
If two players reveal hands of the same type, the player with the higher cards in their hand wins the pot.
If more than one player has the same hand (with no tie-breaker), both players win and the pot is divided evenly amongst them.
When you have no more chips left at the end of a hand, you Bust Out and the game is over.
The game is won when you are the last remaining player at the table. To play again, simply start a new game.
Pass your turn without raising the bet. Can only be done when no other player has RAISED before your turn.
To increase the minimum amount of money other players have to invest in the pot to remain in the hand.

Side pots come into play when an all-in player is unable to contribute as much money to the pot as the remaining players in the hand. In this case, the all-in player is only entitled to the main pot, and a side pot is created for players who have contributed a higher amount of money in the hand.
To put in the amount of money equal to the last bet made before your turn.
To invest all of your remaining money in the pot.

To bow out of the current hand and forfeit your investment in the pot (also known as MUCKING). Once a player has folded, he is not entitled to any winnings from the current hand and cannot take further action until the next hand begins.
The total amount of money the players have contributed for the current hand.
The player who is responsible for dealing out the cards for the current hand.

The cards on the table composed of the FLOP (the first three cards placed face up on the table), the TURN (the forth card placed face up on the table) and the RIVER (the fifth and final card placed face up on the table).
The action of discarding the top card from the deck before dealing the Flop, the Turn and the River.
The first two cards dealt face down to each player.

A forced bet for the first two players at the table (to the left of the Dealer) made before the Hole Cards are dealt. The SMALL BLIND is put in by the first player and the BIG BLIND is put in by the second player. The purpose of the blinds is to add a starting value to the pot that entices players to take action during the hand.

In another moment down went Alice after it, never once considering how in the world she was to get out again.
For some minutes Alice stood without speaking, looking out in all directions over the country - and a most curious country it was.

"What do you mean by that?" said the Caterpillar sternly. "Explain yourself!" "I can't explain myself, I'm afraid, sir," said Alice, "because I'm not myself, you see." "I don't see," said the Caterpillar.
"And round the neck of the bottle was a paper label, with the words "DRINK ME""
"Have you guessed the riddle yet?" the Hatter said, turning to Alice again. "No, I give it up," Alice replied: "what's the answer?" "I haven't the slightest idea," said the Hatter.
"I like the Walrus best," said Alice: "because you see he was a LITTLE sorry for the poor oysters." "He ate more than the Carpenter, though," said Tweedledee.
"Oh, you can't help that," said the cat: "we're all mad here. I'm mad. You're mad." "How do you know I'm mad?" said Alice. "You must be," said the cat, "or you wouldn't have come here."
"Who cares for you?" said Alice, (she had grown to her full size by this time.) "You're nothing but a pack of cards!"
Alice couldn't help laughing, as she said, "I don't want you to hire ME - and I don't care for jam." "It's very good jam," said the Queen.
"Everything's got a moral, if only you can find it."
"And if madness be in the multitude it is in every man, as the quiet lapping of the waves makes up the roar of the sea." - Hobbes

You can tag an enemy or objective for your teammates by keeping an eye on the target and pressing [Tag].
When you're down, press [ClingOnToLife] repeatedly to stay alive and alert nearby teammates of your position.
When your Team Support is ready, you can press [Backup] to trigger it.
Stand next to a box or explosive and press [Interact] to carry it. In this state, you can't sprint, shoot or jump.
You can offer a Booster Shot by pressing [BoosterShot]. To stop offering, press [CancelBuddyboost].
When a teammate offers a Booster Shot, walk up and press[Interact]to select the one you want.
If you don't want to talk to your teammates, just press and hold [TagWheel] to give them commands.
When a dog pins you, you can fend it off with [AttackDog1] and [AttackDog2] to give your teammates time to save you.
If it has a health bar, it can be repaired. Get close and press [EquipRepairTool], then hold [Fire] to repair.
After you carry and set the explosives, you need to find the detonator and use it to make them work.
When a teammate is pinned by a dog, you need to kill the dog to save him.
Aiming with [IronSight] will improve accuracy, but it won't do much for speed.

You can use your machete with [TakeDown].
You can take weapons and ammo left behind by dead enemies.

Aiming with [IronSight] will improve your accuracy by a long shot, but it won't do much for your speed.
You can take weapons and ammo left behind by dead enemies.
Dead enemies don't leave behind grenades. Just weapons and ammo.
You can approach an enemy from behind and press [TakeDown] to kill him stealthily.
No fight is fair. When the time's right, press [Battlecry] to give your teammates a leg up with a Battle Cry.
You can press [Chat] during the game to chat.
You can press [Throw] to throw a grenade.
You can slide under obstacles or behind cover by sprinting and pressing [Crouch].
You can hold [Throw] to cook a grenade, decreasing the time it takes to detonate after you throw it.
You can attach to a zipline simply by jumping onto it.
You can control your speed on a zipline using [ZipSpeed].
You shouldn't ignore a downed teammate. Go up and hold [Revive] to get him back on his feet.
When you're down, you can look around with [Look] to see if there's anyone nearby to revive you.
When your health is low, press and hold [Heal] to heal.
To capture an objective, you need to stay inside the capture area until the meter on the screen is full.
You can't capture an objective if there's an enemy around. Keep the area clear to take it.
To win a Domination match, you need to hold onto the Command Points longer than the other team.
Your minimap will show when a Transmitter is charged and ready for the taking.
There can be more than one working Transmitter at any time. Focusing on one might leave the other open.
It takes a while for a Transmitter to warm up. When it does, the signal strengthens, doubling the points.
Once a Transmitter is captured, it can be stolen again and again until it goes dark.
The bar at the top of the screen shows you how the match is going. Your team is always blue.
The circles on either end of the status bar represent the number of Command Points each team controls.
Once one enemy depot is lit, you need to quickly ignite the other one or the fire will burn out.
If neither team manages to capture the radio, the Firestorm will eventually burn out on its own.
Both teams are playing offense and defense. Ignite the enemy depots while protecting your own.
Once a Firestorm starts, the depots cease to matter. It's all about the mad rush to capture the radio.
If the enemy starts a Firestorm, capturing the radio will reset the match, giving you a second chance.
If your team starts a Firestorm, grabbing the radio will call in a plane to destroy the enemy for good.
The more teammates you have by your side, the faster you can capture an objective.
You can kill an enemy that is capturing an objective to earn bonus XP and Team Support points.
Planting C4 inside of capture areas might be cheap, but it does the trick.
The Killcam displays who killed you and where they did it.
The Killcam tracers point out exactly where you were hit.
War isn't cheap. You need to earn more points to get the best Team Support.
You only earn Team Support points by reviving, using Battle Cries and completing objectives.
If you're lucky enough to get revived, you get to keep your kill streak and all of your Team Support points.
You can choose the type of Team Support you want to use in your Loadout.
You'll earn more XP and Team Support points if your Battle Cry hits a large group.
If you keep dying, Survival Instincts will kick in, giving you the boost you need to make a comeback.
If you kill yourself, you won't have the chance to be revived. So don't kill yourself.
If you're the winning team's top scorer, you get either punish or show mercy to your toughest opponent.
If you want more kills than deaths, cling onto life. Give your teammates a chance to revive you.
You can be revived over and over as long as enough time passes between being saved and getting killed.
You can't kill enemies that are waiting to be revived. You've already done enough.
When you are under the influence of Psych Gas, friends and foes look alike. Watch who you shoot.
When you hit an enemy with armor or extra health, a shield icon will flash under your crosshairs.
You can kill enemies by shooting their own C4 and Proximity Mines.
If you hear faint beeping, you might be about to step on a Proximity Mine.
Using a Battle Cry only affects nearby teammates. In return, you get Team Support points and XP.
Some Loadout options may be good for one game mode but not for another. Try creating a variety.
Get ahead by Decoding! Decoding data like CDs and Hard Drives unlocks XP and unique Weapon Mods.
Completing a Co-op or Multiplayer match earns you Encrypted Data. Decode in-game or online for rewards.
You can review Daily and Weekly Challenges under Profile in the My Setup menu.
You can review your medal progress under Profile in the My Setup menu.
You can view every Weapon Mod under Profile in the My Setup menu, even those you have yet to earn.
You can customize Loadouts and Decode even outside of the game. Go to <website link>.
When you Decode, you may earn a Speed Boost. Give it to a friend to speed up their Decoding time.
In a list from common to rare, you can Decode CDs, Flash Drives, DVDs, Memory Cards and Hard Drives.
You can design a unique tattoo to wear in Multiplayer matches. Just go to My Setup.
You can make your own Multiplayer map for the entire world to play with the Map Editor.
There are three Map Editor playlists. New maps are Bronze, highly rated maps are Silver and the best are Gold.
To get the best Weapon Mods, Decode better data sources like Memory Cards and Hard Drives.
You can give a friend any Weapon Mod that you Decode instead of keeping it for yourself.
Most maps suit any playing style. So choose or make a Loadout that's right for you, not the map.
You can earn XP with a weapon to level it up and unlock new weapon attachments.
Weapon Mods ranks from Mk 1 to Mk 5. A higher number represents a better version of the Weapon Mod.
It's important to stick together. If you're downed or pinned by a dog, you can't exactly rescue yourself.
The big guys can take a lot more bullets than average enemies. Aim for the head and stay out of his way.
There's one Co-op Competition in every chapter. Use this time to show off or vote to skip it.
Take a break and change your Loadout at the Rally Points.
You can't use your machete against a heavy gunner. So don't even try.
If you give a teammate a Booster Shot, you get to pick a shot for yourself too.
Adrenaline shots give you the energy to withstand more pain and take more damage.
Beserker shots improve your close combat resistance, speed and hipfire accuracy.
Stabilizer shots help you snipe the enemy with higher accuracy, better range and less sway.
Amplifier shots make your Battle Cries more frequent, longer reaching and far more powerful.
Energy Burst shots speed up your actions and make you faster on your feet.
Regenerative shots do just what they say. You gain your health back faster in and out of combat.
Leonard's a hard-handed ex-cop from Philadelphia. He has an endless supply of whiskey and cruel jokes.
Mikhail is a Russian ex-con. His 21 tattoos detail his youth, the time he's served, and the men he's killed.
Tisha's an ex-combat medic from Nevada. Now that she's on her own, her med kit isn't exactly regulation.
Callum is a hardened delinquent from Glasgow. He got in his first knife fight when he was six. And won.
The team needs to track down the captain and a means of escape before they can get the stolen cash.
When you give a Booster Shot, you and your teammate will get a bigger boost if you pick the same shot.
Teammates who are carrying boxes or explosives are slow and can't shoot. Watch their backs.
An objective that has a health bar can take damage. If it's destroyed, you'll fail the mission.
Explosive boxes, like ammo boxes, will refill the type of explosives you have in your current Loadout.
Beheaders can't do much from a distance, but one swing of their machetes can put you down.
Shoot a heavy flamer's tank to give him a taste of his own medicine.
Molotov-wielding pirates are impervious to fire. Clearly.
If a teammate is pinned by a dog, an icon will appear. Don't ignore it unless you want to lose a teammate.
The player icons on the left of the screen display your teammates' health and whether they are repairing.
Keeping an eye on the lefthand player icons is a good way to tell when to use Battle Cries.
Mounted guns have massive firepower but are likely to draw attention and leave you vulnerable.
Only enemies can trigger Proximity Mines, but the explosion can hurt anyone nearby. Even you.
Pulling off special techniques like headshots, multi kills, and melee kills will earn you extra XP.
If you have a handgun or flare gun as your secondary weapon, you'll draw it when attached to a zipline.
Tagging can earn you XP. If a teammate kills an enemy that you've tagged, you score points for the assist.
If you can revive a downed teammate, tag him to say you're on the way. He'll be informed if you don't make it.
You can carry less ammo in Multiplayer than in Co-op.
Grenade pouches will give you more grenades in Co-op than in Multiplayer.
You earn more Team Support points if your Battle Cry reaches a lot of teammates.
The "Recovery" Battle Cry gives teammates health regeneration in combat and more out of combat.
The "Toughness" Battle Cry makes your teammates tough to kill by increasing their maximum health.
The "Haste" Battle Cry speeds up your teammates' sprinting, reloading, fire rate and more.
The "Focus" Battle Cry sharpens your teammates' aim.
Needless to say, you take damage when you fall from a large height. Watch your step.
Downed teammates will have icons above their heads. Revive them before they die.
The yellow bar on the left of the minimap is your health. Some boosts, like Battle Cries, can extend the bar.
The number of players that are close enough to hear your Battle Cry is shown next to the Battle Cry icon.
If you have armor in your Loadout, a blue armor bar will appear to the left of your minimap.
When you're in iron sights, icons and name tags will fade away to give you room to aim.
You can't trust a grenade launcher when it's shot from the hip. Aim before you fire.
You shouldn't underestimate handguns. They're fast, effective and pack a decent amount of damage.
Shotguns and sub-machine guns won't slow you down, and they're great up close.
Assault rifles can hit close up and distant targets, but they're the best at medium-range combat.
You can Decode even when you're not in the game. Go to <website link> to get working on those rewards!
You can create and manage your Loadouts online at <website link>.
Decoding will reward you with XP or advanced, customized weapons called Weapon Mods.
Your movement speed depends on which weapon you're carrying.
The speed and angle at which you attach to a zipline affects the speed of your decline and the amount of swing you have. Approach it head on for the best momentum and minimal swing.
The lighter a gun is, the shorter amount of time it takes to switch to iron sights.
While each Battle Cry has a unique effect, all Battle Cries also restore a small amount of your teammates' health.
Hearing two of the same type of Battle Cry doesn't double the effect. Try to coordinate with your team for the best result.
The fire from flamethrowers and Molotovs will burn on the ground for a while. Use this to limit your enemy's movement.
If you don't like healing, Bloodlust is for you. With this skill, you will regenerate health after killing enemies.
The Rock Solid skill prevents you from getting knocked down by explosions, falls and melee attacks.
Different scopes have different advantages. You can't know which one you like best without trying them all.
Not all attachments are equally useful for each weapon. Mix and match until you find your favorite.
Sniper rifles and LMGs are better at shooting through cover than SMGs and shotguns.
Weapon attachments are unlocked in different orders for different weapons.
Check out the Far Cry® 3 Outpost mobile app for Multiplayer and Co-op. Earn Weapon Mods and customize your Loadouts on the go!

When the skydivers approached the island at terminal velocity, it looked like paradise, a lush green dot growing larger in blue Pacific waters. But when Jason and his friends landed, they found hell hiding beneath the jungle canopy. Now Jason must rescue his captured friends from two insane warlords and their numerous soldiers. Luckily, he doesn’t fight alone on an island where "hero" and "hope" have become four-letter words. From a beautiful rebel leader to an unconventional doctor, Jason will need all the help he can get to save his friends, and himself.
Use [Move] to move, and [Aim] to look around.

Press [Fire] to shoot your weapon and [IronSight] to aim down the sights. Different weapons have different firing types, from semi-automatic handguns to fully automatic assault rifles and more. Aiming down the sight of your weapon zooms in your view and gives you more precision.
Press [Throw] to throw a grenade (or molotov, if selected).
Press [Reload] to reload your weapon. Weapons will automatically reload when their clips are empty.
Hold [Interact] when you see the prompt to interact with objects in the world and perform actions such as opening doors, swapping weapons, and picking up items.

Hold [Heal] to heal yourself. If you have medicine, you will heal a large amount of damage quickly. Medicine can be purchased in stores or crafted from the Crafting menu (In the Syringes tab, Medical folder). If you run out of medicine, holding [Heal] will perform First Aid, which heals you for free, but heals you less and takes longer to perform. You can use First Aid to heal as often as you need to.
Click [TakeDown] to perform a melee attack with your machete.
Once you begin to learn the powerful Takedown skills from the Skills menu, you can press [TakeDown] when prompted to kill enemies quickly and silently.
Hold [GadgetWheel] to open the weapon selector. Use [WeaponWheelSelect] to select a gun, grenade type, or explosive type, and release [GadgetWheel] to equip it.

Press [SwitchWeapon] to swap your current weapon with the previous one. Note: at the start of the game, you can only carry one weapon. You will be able to carry more weapons by crafting Weapon Holsters in the Crafting menu.
Click [Run] while moving to sprint. You will sprint quickly at first and then slow to a steady jogging pace. You can also click [Run] while swimming to swim faster.
Press [Crouch] to crouch. When crouched, you make less noise when moving, and enemies have a harder time detecting you.
Press [Climb] when you see the on-screen prompt to begin climbing an object. Use [MoveUpDown] to climb up and down.
Press [EquipCamera] to equip or holster your camera. See the Controls - Camera section for more details.
Press [ThrowRock] to throw a rock. Rocks create noise, which can distract enemies. Use this opportunity to sneak past them, or sneak up on them and kill them with a Takedown.

In the Crafting menu, you can assign syringes or special arrows you have crafted to the [AssignLeft] or [AssignDown] shortcuts. When in-game, press [AssignLeft] or [AssignDown] to use that syringe immediately.
Press [Start] to pause the game and view the Skills, Crafting, Loot Rucksack, and Handbook menus.
The World Map and Menu Shortcuts
Press [WorldMap] to open the World Map. Sometimes [Back] is also used as a shortcut to access other menus - look for the on-screen prompts.
Hold [HoldEnterExit] to enter or exit a vehicle. If a vehicle is moving when you exit, you may get hurt.
Hold [Accelerate] to accelerate and hold [Brake] to brake. When a vehicle is stopped, hold [Brake] to reverse.
Use [Steer] to steer a vehicle left and right.
Hold [HandBrake] to handbrake and make a vehicle come to a complete stop. Handbrake at high speeds to drift.
Use [Look] to look around while in a vehicle. Hold [LookDown] to look behind you.
Press [SwitchSeats] to switch between the driver's seat and the mounted gun (in supported vehicles only).
Press [Radio] to turn the radio on or off.
Press [NextSong] for next song.
Hold [HoldEnterExit] to board a glider. You will automatically launch the glider and begin flying.
Use [Steer] to change the pitch of a glider or to steer it left and right.
Use [Look] to look around while gliding.

Use [Move] to move the glider close enough to the ground with a straight angle of approach and you will exit automatically. If your angle of approach is too steep, you may crash the glider and get hurt. You can bail in mid-air by holding [Interact] but if you fall too far you may get hurt or die.

After you acquire a wingsuit, press [Wingsuit] to deploy it when freefalling from a high altitude. Use [Steer] to pitch and steer yourself in the air. You must deploy your parachute to land safely, otherwise you may get hurt or die.
When you reach a lower altitude in a wingsuit, press [Parachute] when prompted to deploy your parachute. Use [Move] to turn, and to control your rate of descent to land safely.
Press [EquipCamera] to equip or holster your camera. The camera is mainly used to tag and track enemies, and to take pictures to complete mission objectives.
Use [Look] to aim the camera.
Press [ZoomIn] and [ZoomOut] to zoom in and out when using the camera.

To tag enemies or animals, center your camera viewfinder on them and zoom in until you see the tag icon automatically appear over their heads. The tags will remain visible until you move too far away, or until you kill the tagged enemy or animal. The tags are visible through solid objects and let you safely track your targets from a distance.

Press [TakePicture] when prompted to take a picture with the camera (during missions that require you to photograph something). The prompt will only appear when your subject is properly framed. To properly frame a subject, center it in your viewfinder and then zoom in until the on-screen prompt tells you to press [TakePicture] to take the picture.
Use [Move] to move while in camera mode. Note: you will move at a reduced speed.
Press [NewsFeed] to switch to the News Feed.
Press [MenuUp] and [MenuDown] to move the cursor up and down the news feed.

Control schemes can be changed in the Options menu. In the main menu, go to Options, Controls, and choose Control scheme. In the game, open the pause menu with [Start] then choose Options, Controls, and Control Scheme.

This is the current task you have to complete in order to progress further through the game. You can review your objective at any time in the pause menu. It is displayed in the top left corner. New missions and quests, as well as the current objective, can be found on the Map.
Hints and additional information about your current objective will be displayed here.
This appears when you start a new mission.
This message box informs you when: A new tutorial is available New game content is unlocked There is an important message
Displays how much money you have.
As you earn Experience Points, the XP bar will fill up. When full, you are granted a skill point to spend in the Skills menu.
Your crosshair shows what you are aiming at, and indicates your general level of accuracy with a weapon. It will turn red when aiming at an enemy, and green when aiming at an ally.

This appears around your crosshair when enemies begin to detect you. The closer they are to spotting you, the more it will fill up. When full, it will flash to show that you have been spotted. It turns red when you are attacked and injured by an enemy.
The yellow bars show how much health you have left. The blue bar represents the strength of your body armor.
Shows which weapon is currently equipped and the amount of bullets in its magazine. To the left is the crouch indicator, which appears when you are crouched.
Shows which throwable weapon you have equipped (grenades or molotovs), and how many you have.
The minimap displays: Nearby terrain (if you have activated the local radio tower) Important locations (displayed as icons) North indicator (compass)
Shows the location of grenades that enemies have thrown at you.
Appears whenever the game is saved, or when you reach a mission checkpoint.
Displays the subtitles, for most spoken dialog when the subtitle option is enabled.

The distance indicator shows the distance in meters to your current objective or waypoint. The flashing arrow next to the indicator shows if the objective is above or below you. The medicine indicator in the bottom left shows how many uses of medicine you have left.
Gameplay prompts tell you which action will be performed.
Appears when you pick up an important item, gather a plant, skin an animal, or loot a body.
Displays a timer or counter, depending on your current objective.
When you place a Waypoint on the World Map, this indicator will show you its direction and location in the world.
Use your camera to tag and track both enemies and animals. Aim and zoom at your target to tag it automatically. Each type of enemy and animal has its own icon.
Normal - regular enemy types
Charger - aggressive enemies that charge at you
Heavy - strong, heavily armored enemies
Sniper/RPG - enemies that attack from long range
Herbivores - any non-aggressive animal that can be hunted for its skin
Predators - dangerous animals that attack on sight

Your battles, your way - this is the motto of Far Cry® 3 . As you explore Rook Island, you will engage in many battles. How you approach them is entirely up to you. There is no wrong way to play. Whether you prefer to snipe your enemies from long range, close in stealthily with suppressed weapons, or engage in brutal direct assaults, Far Cry® 3 has you covered. Most encounters will let you approach the battlefield from any angle - even from the air. Use your camera to tag enemies in advance and track their positions. Use rocks to create distractions and sneak past enemies. Craft syringes to give you temporary boosts in battle. Start strategic fires with molotovs, flamethrowers or flare guns. Cause havoc with remotely detonated C4 charges or proximity mines. Learn powerful takedown skills to kill your enemies instantly. Customize your weapons with a variety of scopes, magazines, sound suppressors and paint jobs. The choices are many, but they're yours to make. Welcome to Far Cry® 3 .

Your game is saved automatically and often. Whenever you see the savegame indicator appear on-screen, your progress is being saved. When you are in a mission, the checkpoint indicator will appear in the same place. You can also save manually from the pause menu by choosing the Save option (when available). You should do this regularly. If you die during a mission, you will restart at the nearest checkpoint in that mission and lose the progress you made since that checkpoint. If you die while exploring the world between missions, you will continue at the nearest liberated outpost or activated radio tower without penalty.

Your health is shown around the minimap as a series of yellow bars. As you take damage, the bars will drain. Your health regenerates the nearest partially-depleted bar, but you can only heal empty bars by holding [Heal] to use medicine. If you run out of syringes, you can still hold [Heal] heal for free at any time, which will trigger First Aid, but this is slower than other methods and does not recover as much health. Several skills can be learned in the Skills menu that will give you more health bars. Other skills can speed up health regeneration and boost your defenses. You can buy medicine in stores, but you can also craft them yourself from the Syringes tab in the Crafting menu. Syringes are stored in your Syringe Kit, which has limited space, but you can also craft larger Syringe Kits once you have the correct recipe. You should also buy body armor when possible to give yourself an additional layer of protection.

You'll spend most of your time in Far Cry® 3 getting in or out of firefights. Here are some of the ways you can keep the situation under control. Check your detection meter. When enemies start to detect you, don't be afraid to fall back and find another way through, or create a distraction by throwing a rock. Use cover. If it looks like you can hide behind it, you can probably use it as cover. Stay crouched, and don't forget to check out the situation by using [IronSight] to quickly peek out around edges and corners. Look for opportunities. Keep an eye out for vantage points, ziplines, getaway vehicles, explosive fuel drums and cover points as you prepare for battle. Track your enemies. You can tag enemies from a distance with your camera, or tag up close by aiming at them with [IronSight] when they are within the optimal range of your weapon. Stay healthy. Keep a supply of medical syringes for quick healing, or be prepared to take the time to perform First Aid.

When you crouch, you automatically become more stealthy by reducing your visibility and making less noise when moving. Playing stealthily has many advantages. You can reduce enemy numbers without alerting everyone nearby, hunt animals that would otherwise flee at your presence, and earn XP rewards for using takedowns or liberating outposts without sounding alarms.

Keep track of the detection meter around your crosshair. When enemies begin to detect you, it will start to fill up. You can track the location and the detection rate of up to 3 nearby enemies. When you have been spotted, the meter will flash and remain on screen.

There are plenty of weapons and tools at your disposal to aid stealthy gameplay: Many handguns, SMGs and sniper rifles support sound suppressor attachments for near-silent weapon kills. The recurve bow is a deadly weapon that often kills enemies with just one arrow in complete silence. Throwing rocks with [ThrowRock] can create noise that will distract enemies and allow you to sneak past them or sneak up on them. Tag enemies with the camera to track their position as you sneak around them. Craft the Sharpshooter or Enhanced Perception syringes for additional advantages.

There are several skills you can learn from the Skills menu. These skills can give you powerful takedown moves that let you kill quickly and silently, reduce the noise you make when moving, and give you many other valuable advantages.

If you are spotted, all is not lost. You can regain your stealth by breaking your enemy's line of sight to you for a period of time. Use cover, thick vegetation, and pools and rivers to hide in. Also, remain crouched when you move where possible. Don't be afraid to pull back and try again with different tactics if your first attempt fails.

As you progress on your journey, you will earn experience points (XP) for many actions. Earn enough XP and you will be granted a skill point to spend in the Skills menu. Each time you learn a skill, it will be represented on your left arm as a tattoo, or “tatau”, as the Rakyat people of Rook Island call it. You can learn skills from 3 different paths. New skills will be made available as you progress through the story.
Heron skills are focused on long range attacks, improved mobility, weapons use, and takedowns from above and below enemies.
Skills in this path are split between aggressive, powerful takedowns, and skills that boost your health, defenses and damage recovery.
The Spider path contains skills that improve your stealth abilities and survival skills that support hunting, looting, and weapon handling.

XP is awarded for many actions. Here is a summary of the main XP rewards that can be earned: Activate a radio tower: 500 XP Liberate an outpost: 500 XP Liberate an outpost without sounding any alarms: 550 XP Liberate an outpost without being detected: 1500 XP Collect a Relic: 250 XP Collect a Letter of the Lost: 500 XP Kill a pirate: 10 XP Kill a heavy class pirate: 50 XP Headshot kill an enemy: XP x2 Standard takedown kill: XP x3 Death from above kill: XP x5 Death from below kill: XP x5 Dual death from above kill: XP x7.5 per kill Dual death from below kill: XP x7.5 per kill Gunslinger takedown kill: XP x3 for the first kill, then XP x5 for each handgun victim Knife throw takedown kill: XP x3 for the first kill, then XP x5 for the knife throw victim Heavy beatdown kill: XP x5 Grenade takedown kill: XP x3 for the first kill, then XP x5 for every enemy killed by the grenade. Chained takedown kill: XP x3 for the first kill, then XP x10 for every other kill.

Soon after beginning your journey, you will learn how to craft items. Crafting requires ingredients and a recipe. Gathering plants gives you ingredients to craft syringes that can heal you, or enhance your abilities for a limited time. Hunting animals and skinning them gives you the ingredients you need to make new, larger bags and holsters to carry more weapons, ammo and other equipment. New recipes will be unlocked as you complete missions and meet other requirements. Some recipes will be unlocked when you complete other recipes in a sequence. In the Crafting menu, recipes are divided into four categories.

Use animal skins to craft weapon holsters for carrying more guns. You can also make wallets to carry more money, loot rucksacks to carry more loot, and syringe kits to carry more syringes. When you craft equipment, its effects are applied immediately and permanently.

Syringes come in many varieties. Medical syringes can heal you. Exploration, Combat and Hunting syringes improve your abilities to move, observe, and fight. When you craft a syringe, you can use it directly from the Crafting menu, or assign it as a shortcut. Most syringes are time-limited when used. The duration of a syringe’s effects is displayed on-screen when you use it. The effects of one syringe are cancelled when you use another.
Use animal skins to craft larger bag and pouches to carry more ammunition for your weapons.

Use animal skins to make larger quivers for carrying more arrows. Additionally you can make explosive and fire-tipped arrow tips for strategic use in combat and hunting.

When you craft an arrow tip, you can use it directly from the Crafting menu (if you have a bow), or assign it as a shortcut.

You can loot the bodies of your enemies for money, ammo, and items to sell. Your loot items are stored in your Loot Rucksack, which you can check in the pause menu. You can sort the items, or permanently discard items you don't want. When your Loot Rucksack is full, you should sell unwanted items at stores. Increase the amount of loot you can carry by crafting a larger Loot Rucksack in the Crafting menu.

Dead animals can be skinned in order to obtain ingredients for crafting. Animal skins are used to craft larger ammo bags as well as items that allow you to carry more weapons, money, loot, and syringes.
Plant leaves can be gathered to craft syringes that boost your abilities temporarily. Plants are categorized by color and are revealed on the minimap after you activate radio towers.

A large array of weapons are available on Rook Island. You can find basic weapons on the bodies of your enemies. Activating radio towers scattered across the island will make weapons become free in stores.
Handguns are most efficient at short range. Ammo is readily available and the reload times are short.
SMGs (submachine guns) are fully automatic weapons which burn through ammo quickly.
You should always carry a good assault rifle. They offer solid performance in mid-range combat situations.
Shotguns can be devastating at close range, but suffer from long reload times. A good strategy is to keep moving and use cover.
LMGs (light machine guns) provide sustained firepower and large clip sizes. Use them to attack large groups of enemies, but beware of long reload times and limited mobility when firing.
The RPG-7 and GL-94 can deliver powerful explosives from mid-range, but have limited ammo and are very slow to reload. The best strategy is to fire from safety and move on quickly.
Sniper rifles are the long range weapon of choice. Some sniper rifles support powerful scopes and sound suppressors, but are not suitable for close range combat.

Grenades and molotovs can be thrown from medium distances and can scatter enemies, start fires, or just bring a little chaos into battle. C4 is a remotely detonated explosive, great for lying in wait for vehicles or patrols. Proximity mines can be used to fortify your position or cover your tracks from pursuing enemies.

The recurve bow is the perfect weapon for stealthy players. Arrows are lethal and silent. Fire tips and explosive tips are also available for your arrows. The flamethrower is large and heavy, but devastatingly destructive. It is capable of burning everything in its path. The flare gun is great for starting fires at precise locations and can be used on ziplines. The repair tool is used to repairing damaged vehicles, but it can also be used as a weapon if you're in a tight spot.

More powerful weapons support attachments of different varieties, from scopes and sound suppressors to larger magazines and various sights. Customize weapons with attachments and paint jobs at stores and make your weapons your own.
You'll encounter a lot of hostility on Rook Island, especially from Vaas and his pirates.
Assaulters are common thugs armed with basic weaponry. They are a force to be reckoned with when in large numbers.
Defenders can soak up more bullets thanks to their light armor.
Armed with only a machete, these unstable individuals will make a run straight for you. Take them out quick.
Armed with powerful short range weapons, these troops will move in close before trying to punch through your defenses.
Permanently high on their own supply, these pyromaniacs need no excuse to start a fire.
Bred in large numbers by Vaas's pirates, these dogs are extremely aggressive and have been trained to kill on sight. Locals claim that they are sometimes fed with human flesh.
Armed with a brutal light machine gun and heavily armored, these men are the embodiment of terror. Take them on if you dare.
Clad in heavy fireproof armor, these men are as strong as oxes and take great pleasure in burning everything they can to a fiery crisp. Countless civilians have died at their hands.
These long range specialists support their allies from a distance with high caliber sniper rifles. Keep an eye out for their telltale laser sights.
Armed with RPG-7 weapons, these guys are technically anti-armor troops, but with an absence of tanks on Rook Island, they're just happy to blow shit up.

You will have many opportunities to explore Rook Island, either between missions or when travelling to your next objective. Activate radio towers and liberate outposts. This is the quickest way to unlock new quests and activities. You'll also reveal the map and make the island safer. Hunt animals and gather plants, and use their ingredients for crafting equipment, special arrow tips, or syringes. Search for collectible items to get bonus XP, money, and other items. Visit stores regularly. Take some time out to sell your loot, buy new weapons, try a new weapon loadout, or customize weapons with attachments and paint jobs.

Radio towers are spread across the island, forming a communication network. Vaas' pirates installed scramblers that block their signals. Activate them to reveal the map terrain, and make weapons free in stores.

Outposts are enemy camps located across the island that control the local enemy presence. Kill all the enemies at an outpost to liberate it. Look for their black smoke stacks and red flags to find them.

Many outposts have one or more alarms that can be triggered, leading to the arrival of enemy reinforcements. You can manually disable an alarm by interacting with it, which will turn off all alarms in the outpost. You can also destroy an alarm by shooting at it, but this will alert nearby enemies and will not disable other alarms in the area. An alerted enemy will try to trigger an alarm if he can. If he succeeds, reinforcements will come, which will make liberating the outpost more difficult. If you manage to liberate an outpost without sounding an alarm, you will receive an XP bonus. If you liberate an outpost without being detected at all, you'll get a larger bonus.

When an outpost is liberated, the Rakyat will come to take it over. This will unlock new activities and quests. Also, the region controlled by the outpost will become friendly, reducing the amount of enemies you'll encounter there.

Each outpost contains a safe house. Once liberated, you can use the safe house as a fast travel point. Inside each safe house is an automated store to purchase, equip, and customize weapons with attachments.
Regions that are controlled by outposts are colored red on the world map. These areas will clear up as you liberate outposts.
Liberated outposts can be used for fast travel. Open the World map with [WorldMap] then move the map cursor over a liberated outpost, and press [Accept] to fast travel there.

Stores are usually found in villages and other safe areas. You can buy weapons, ammo, medicine, maps and more, and also customize your weapons with attachments and paint jobs. Automated stores will become available each time you liberate an outpost. Weapons have a cost, but are made free as you activate radio towers.
You can sell items you've collected in your loot rucksack. Rarer items will fetch a good price, but some items should be kept for crafting.

Far Cry® 3 ’s in-game currency, denominated "Dollars" or "American Dollars", is not an actual currency or any type of financial instrument, and is not redeemable for any sum of money from Ubisoft at any time.
Memory cards are found in abandoned laptops across the island and contain information about the local drug trade. Finding them will earn you money and items.
The Rakyat people have placed, lost, or left behind many relics across the island over the years. Finding them all will be a test of skill and commitment.

Remnants of the Japanese occupation of Rook Island during WWII still exist today, including several letters that were never delivered. They can be found by anyone brave enough to pluck them from the corpses of their mummified owners.

Maps can be purchased at stores and come in two types: maps which show the locations of collectible items, and maps for loot chests. Once purchased, these items will appear on the world map, but only if you've activated the radio tower in the region first. New maps will be unlocked as you progress through the story.

These Trials will have you gunning for a high score by taking out waves of enemy troops within a time limit, with a fixed set of weapons. The Trials are available at any time while you are exploring the island. Look for the icons on the map, where you can press [TabRight] to access more info about them. The Trials are located at large colored rocks with the name of the highest scoring player written as graffiti on it. Once you've beaten each challenge, you can continue to take part in them and maintain your ranking on the online leaderboard.

Support the Rakyat people by completing these quests. Story quests are unlocked as you progress through story, and complement the main story with new characters and narrative insight. Other quest types are unlocked by activating radio towers and liberating outposts, and are detailed below.
The Rakyat need you to take out the most dangerous men on Rook Island. Find your targets and kill them.
Earn respect among the Rakyat by hunting dangerous wildlife.
Transport supplies in vehicles to the Rakyat people who need them the most.
As you liberate outposts, new activities will be unlocked. These games and challenges have a cost of entry.
A simple game played by the locals. Toss the ball in the hole, or take shot of beer. Taunt your opponent to miss, and don't pass out.
A few locations on Rook Island invite gun enthusiasts to participate in shooting challenges, with a cost of entry. Each location has a weapon of choice and a score to beat in the time allotted.
The variety of topography Rook Island offers is perfect for these racing challenges. Buckle up and race to the finish line in the time allotted to win.

The Rakyat people of Rook Island are proud and skillful hunters. This is particularly true when they demonstrate their knife throwing abilities. Try to accumulate a better score than your opponent by throwing the knife as close to the center of the target as possible.

For some this is a pleasant diversion, for others, a religion. One thing's for sure: poker made its way to Rook Island and it's there to stay. It's the fastest way to lose money, but a good earner for skilled players. Bet carefully.

Pirates roam the island to establish their dominance, patrolling on foot or in vehicles, defending areas, taking hostages, or committing random acts of violence. If they see you, they'll shoot first and ask questions later. If you're able to rescue their victims you'll surely be rewarded. As you liberate outposts, the pirate presence in the local area will diminish and you will encounter less of them on your travels.

When a twisted ship captain sells his black market cruise liner and everyone on it to a warlord named Hoyt, only four crewmembers have the courage to fight back. They band together to fight off the pirates and recover the safe that holds the ship's profits and the crew's earnings. But the captain has different plans in mind. He escapes, taking the money from the safe with him, and takes refuge on Hoyt's island. Now, the four survivors must claw their way through the jungle to reclaim what they have lost and exact revenge against the man who wronged them.

Growing up in the projects of Glasgow, Callum developed an early attachment to knives. At six, he won his first knife fight. At 12, he was already leading a street gang of his own. After years of dodging serious trouble, Callum’s ruthless spirit finally took its toll. He picked a fight with the wrong man, snapped and incidentally beat him to a pulp. Hunted by police and gang members, he fled Scotland and found a job on the SS Astrid. Callum has a cynical, black-humored point of view, but becomes aggressive, ruthless and, at times, psychotic when provoked.

Leonard started out like any other cop in Philly: a good Catholic boy, following in his father's footsteps. But as he climbed the ranks, his ethics dimmed. He planted evidence, stole from busts, and wasn’t above negotiating a favor from a hot blonde in place of a ticket. Leonard got things done, no matter what. But in the end, his loose definition of the rules cost him his gun and badge. A cop buddy pulled a few strings to land him a security gig on board the SS Astrid. In battle, he's the top of the food chain. He fights with his gut and will use any excuse to crack a vulgar joke.

In her home outside of Las Vegas, Tisha learned to take charge from an early age. Her binge-drinking mother and absent father left her the head of the household, and she’s been a leader ever since. Tisha joined the army as a combat medic straight out of high school and was respected for her aggressive and focused personality. After four tours overseas, a commanding officer with a personal grudge managed to get her diagnosed with a pre-existing personality disorder, although knocking him out might have had something to do with it. She was booted without benefits. Embittered and sick of home, she found a job on a website for remote medics on board the SS Astrid. Now that she's back in the fight, she finds herself more suited to guns than needles and ruthlessly takes on the enemy face-to-face without hesitation.

As a street orphan in St. Petersburg, Mikhail’s youth was marked with abuse and abandonment. It wasn’t until his teenage years that he found his path and fell in with an elite league of criminals, known for its strict code of conduct that extolled honor and resistance against authority. After two stints in jail and years of devotion, he was crowned a leader of his gang and became the right-hand man to his mentor. But when he fell in love and eloped, breaking his league’s code, he was forced to flee and put his wife, Katya, and newborn daughter into hiding. Now he's working aboard the SS Astrid to earn what money he can to start a new life outside of Russia. Always one step ahead, he’s calm and collected in battle. His mercy extends to no one.

TEAMS: 2 Multiplayer includes four team-based game modes: Domination, Firestorm, Transmission and Team Deathmatch. Choose Quick Match to jump right into the action or set up a Custom Match to fine-tune the game the way you want. You can even create your own map in the Map Editor or play other user-made maps by browsing the Map Editor Archive or trying out the Map Editor Playlists.

Dominate the other team by capturing and holding the Command Points. The team that holds the Command Points for the longest cumulative time wins. There are three Command Points, each with its own unique name. Each Command Point is marked with a flare. Stay close to the flare to capture the point. If there's an enemy inside the capture area, you can't capture the point. Clear the area of enemies to continue capturing. The bar at the top of the screen shows the status of the fight. Your team is always blue. The blue circles represent the Command Points that are currently under your control. The red ones represent the points that are under the enemy's control. The more blue, the better.

Each team has two supply depots. Your job is to trigger a firestorm and destroy your enemy's supplies while protecting your own. In other words, both teams play offense and defense at the same time. Firestorm is a two stage process. In the first stage, your team needs to ignite the enemy's supplies. Interact with an enemy supply depot to set it on fire. Once you've ignited the first depot, you have a short time to ignite the second depot before the first burns out. When a team manages to ignite both of its enemy's supply depots simultaneously, a firestorm is triggered and the second stage begins. A radio will activate in the middle of the map, and it's an all-out brawl to see which team can capture it first. As in Domination, you need to remain in the capture area to get the radio. You can't capture the radio if the area is contested. If the team that triggered the firestorm captures the radio, a plane will dump gasoline onto the area, igniting the rest of the map and ending the game. If the team that didn't trigger the firestorm captures the radio, a plane will dump water onto the area, quenching the flames and resetting the match to the first stage. In summary, ignite the enemy supply depots simultaneously and then capture the radio to win the game.

Vaas and Citra want their voices heard, and they're sending their soldiers onto the field to make sure it's done. Several transmitters are scattered across the map. Your team needs to take the transmitters and hold them the longest to win. Your minimap will highlight the transmitters that are active. Capture an active transmitter by remaining in its capture area. The transmitter can't be captured if the area is contested. Once you control the transmitter, you start scoring points. After a while, the transmitter will heat up, broadcasting louder and doubling the points given. If you lose the transmitter to an enemy, don't worry. The transmitter can be captured again and again until it overheats and goes dark.

The rules are simple. Kill more enemies than they can kill of you. The team with the highest number of kills wins the match. There's one caveat. Each time you revive a teammate, a point is subtracted from the enemy team. Stick together and keep reviving.
Press [Fire] to shoot your weapon.
Press [IronSight] to aim down the sights of your weapon. Aiming will give you more precision.
Press [Throw] to throw a grenade or molotov if included in your current Loadout.
Press [Reload] to reload your weapon. Weapons will automatically reload when their clips are empty.
Hold [Interact] when you see the prompt to interact with objects in the world and perform actions such as opening doors, swapping weapons, and picking up items.
Hold [Heal] to heal yourself when your health is critical.
Press [TakeDown] to perform a melee attack with your machete.
Hold [HoldWeaponInv] to open the weapon selector.
Press [SwitchWeapon] to swap your current weapon with the previous one.
Press [Run] while moving to sprint. You can also press [Run] while swimming to swim faster.
Press [Crouch] to crouch. When crouched, you make less noise when moving, and enemies have a harder time detecting you.
Press [Climb] when you see the on-screen prompt to climb an object.
Press [Battlecry1] + [Battlecry2] to use your Battle Cry. Battle Cries enhance the abilities of surrounding teammates. Equip different Battle Cries in your Loadout.
Press [Battlecry] to use your Battle Cry. Battle Cries enhance the abilities of surrounding teammates. Equip different Battle Cries in your Loadout.
Press [Revive] to revive a downed teammate.
Press [ClingOnToLife] repeatedly to stay alive until a teammate can revive you. (Multiplayer Only)
Press [Backup] to use Team Support. You can equip different Team Supports in your Loadout. (Multiplayer Only)
Press [TagWheel] to bring up the Tag Wheel. Use the Tag Wheel to give commands to your teammates.
Press [Tag] to tag enemies and objectives. You can also tag downed teammates to let them know you're coming to revive them.
Press [EquipRepairTool] to take out your repair tool and hold [Fire] to repair. (Co-op Only)
Press [BoosterShot] to offer a Booster Shot. To accept a Booster Shot, walk up to the teammate offering and press[Interact]. (Co-op Only)
